en: The Scripture on the Divine Incantations Spoken by the Venerable Bhadra, as Taught by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Tanwulan of India during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was traveling through the kingdom of Rājagṛha, staying among the śukas (parrots) trees.
At that time, there was a certain bhikṣu who,
while traveling from the Bamboo Grove toward the city of Rājagṛha,
was bitten by a snake in the midst of his journey.
Furthermore, he was possessed by malevolent spirits and plundered by bandits;
upon seeing the Buddha, he immediately went to where that bhikṣu was.
At that time, the Master Xuan Bada followed the Buddha and went along with him.
Master Xuan Bada then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I possess a most marvelous art; I now wish to perform a spell for you."
The Buddha said, "Stop, stop, Bhadra!
Do not let your incantations cause any harm.
Bhadra addressed the Buddha, saying:
In the future, states will attack one another;
thieves will plunder one another;
and those who increase their own power will, in turn, plunder one another.
During the kalpa of spirits and ghosts,
poisons and venomous creatures harm one another.
If there is a bhikṣu sitting beneath a tree in the mountains...
Whether wearing the fivefold patched robe or sitting in the open air, I shall ensure that none among the fourfold assembly of disciples shall harm me;
I shall cause them all to be secure and free from illness. Thus it shall be.
Saṃghe svāhā | Nīrucchale śūlibhadre | Saṃyukte pibadane | With this mantra,
one cuts off speech, cuts off all delusions, and cuts off all illnesses and pains.
All these yakṣas became thus deluded: Sumatu, Mahā-ekayodhana, Mahā-yakṣabrahma, Yodha-mahā-yakṣa, Indrā-kīrmahā-yakṣa, and Aghipa-mahā-yakṣa.
These yakṣas are the most honored among the spirits and ghosts.
My name is Indu; for those afflicted by the diseases of desire and those who harm others, I cause them all to be unaware of the person's location.
"I shall shroud your eyes so that you cannot see anyone,
ensuring that no one can take advantage of you.
At that time, you should call out:"
Come! Rākṣasa spirits, come! Mahārākṣasa spirits, come!

Tukhāra, Mahātukhāra, Indratukhāra, Come-Brahmā, Mahātukhāra, Mahābrahmā-tukhāra, Come-Yakṣa-tukhāra, Hata, Da, Tukhāra, Śūra-kuśa-tukhāra, Mahāśūra-kuśa-tukhāra—those whose names begin with *Indu*, all you enemies who seek an opportunity against me, I shall protect them all; I shall shield them so that the two may not see one another.
Bound by ropes and cords,
bound by shackles and fetters,
and bound by a distracted mind.
All together take refuge in the Buddha; all shall be liberated.
Homage to the Buddha! At that time, Namo Buddha brings great auspiciousness.
This is the *Buddhabhāṣita-vidyāmantra-sūtra* spoken by the Great Master Bhadra.
